cues.en: Your brain is two brains, two hemispheres, each doing half the work of being you. Half your vision goes to each and half your movement directed by each. Right controls left and left controls right. Your two brains coordinate through a wire of nerves, but this wire can be cut and was, for a time, used
cues.zh: 你的大脑其实是两个大脑，也就是两个半球，各自承担了构成“你”的一半工作。两边各接收一半的视野，各控制一半的动作。右脑控制左半身，左脑控制右半身。你的两个大脑通过一条神经线路协调工作，但这条线路是可以被切断的，而且曾经有一段时间被用作

cues.en: as an epilepsy treatment. After the cut, people seemed the same, though their brain was split in twain. Except some post-split patients described that while selecting their morning outfit with right hand, left might come along to disagree. Actually, left hand might quite often disagree, which these split brain patients found frustrating. What's happening? To investigate, remember, right brain sees and controls one half while left brain controls and sees the other. But only left brain can speak. Hello.
cues.zh: 癫痫的治疗手段。切断之后，虽然大脑一分为二，但人们看起来并无异样。除了一些术后患者描述说，当右手在挑选早晨穿的衣服时，左手可能会跑过来反对。实际上，左手常常唱反调，这让裂脑患者感到很沮丧。这是怎么回事？为了探究原因，请记住：右脑负责看并控制一侧，而左脑控制并看到另一侧。但只有左脑能说话。“你好。”

cues.en: Because that's where the speech center is located. Right brain without this is mute. In normal brains, this doesn't matter because each half communicates across the wire with the other. But split brains can't and thus you can show just the right brain a word. Ask the person what did you see and you'll hear nothing. Because left speaking brain saw nothing. Meanwhile, right brain will use its hand to pick the object out of a pile hidden from left brain. This is deeply creepy.
cues.zh: 因为语言中枢就在左脑。没有这个中枢的右脑是个哑巴。在正常大脑中，这无关紧要，因为两半球可以通过那根神经线彼此沟通。但裂脑患者做不到，所以你可以只给右脑看一个词。问这个人看到了什么，你会听到“什么也没看到”。因为负责说话的左脑确实什么都没看见。与此同时，右脑会用它的手在左脑看不到的一堆东西里挑出那个物体。这让人不寒而栗。

cues.en: Ask why are you holding the object and speaking left brain will make up a plausible sounding but totally wrong reason. I always wanted to learn how to solve one of these.
cues.zh: 如果问“你为什么拿着这个东西？”，负责说话的左脑会编造出一个听起来合理但完全错误的理由。“我一直都想学会怎么解开这种东西。”

cues.en: Left brain isn't lying, it's just doing what brains do, creating a story that explains its past actions to its current self. A behavior which does rather cast doubt onto the notion of free will, but that's a story for another time. Creating reasons for why it does things is just something left brains do. It happens in normal, healthy humans all the time, and if you think about it closely, you know you've done this. Back to experiments. Give right brain an object, ask the person what's in your hand, and they won't be able to say.
cues.zh: 左脑并不是在撒谎，它只是在做大脑常做的事：编造一个故事，向当下的自己解释过去的行动。这种行为确实让人对“自由意志”的概念产生了怀疑，不过那是另一个话题了。为自己的所作所为找借口，正是左脑的拿手好戏。在正常、健康的人身上这种事一直在发生，如果你仔细想想，就会发现自己也做过。回到实验中来。给右脑一个物体，问这个人手里拿的是什么，他们什么也说不

cues.en: anything. And when asked to draw a split brain can draw two separate objects simultaneously with each hand in a way unsplit brains find challenging. These experiments on split brain patients are deeply unsettling because they really point in the direction of a mute separate intelligence something living in the skull. You can even ask questions of a split brain and get disagreement on the answer. So if your brain is split
cues.zh: 出来。而且当要求画画时，裂脑患者能双手同时画出两个不同的物体，这种能力在未做手术的人看来极为困难。这些针对裂脑患者的实验令人深感不安，因为它们明确指向了一个不会说话的独立智慧体——一个活在头骨深处的东西。你甚至可以向裂脑提问，并得到截然相反的答案。那么如果你的大脑被分开了，

cues.en: Who is the you in this situation?
cues.zh: 在这种情况下，到底谁才是“你”？

cues.en: From the outside, it's tempting to think of the part of the brain that's speaking as the person, but something is hearing and answering questions. And though right brain can't speak, it does understand faces, which left brain can't. If this is you, you don't know who your friends and family are in a crowd. This act of cutting exposes two minds in one head, and the talking mind doesn't know there's someone else in the house. The left brain can describe the situation
cues.zh: 从外表看，人们很容易把大脑负责说话的部分当作这个人本身，但其实还有另一个存在正在聆听并回答问题。虽然右脑不会说话，但它能识别面孔，而左脑不行。如果左脑就是你，你在人群中连自己的亲朋好友都认不出来。这切断的一刀揭示了一个头颅里的两个心智，而且那个会说话的心智根本不知道屋里还有别人。左脑可以描述它所处的

cues.en: It's in but nonetheless will constantly be surprised by right brains actions and explain them away There's a question to be asked here. Why after separation does right brain not totally freak out? But instead plays along helpfully answering questions and listening to left brains dumb stories about what's happening. It's the best pony I don't know speculation time But one answer is the cutting doesn't make right brain a separate intelligence consciousness
cues.zh: 处境，但仍会不断被右脑的举动吓一跳，并找借口敷衍过去。这里有个问题：为什么分开后，右脑没有彻底抓狂？反而配合地帮忙回答问题，还听着左脑胡扯刚才发生了什么。“这是最棒的小马。”我不知道，现在是推测时间。但有一种答案是：那一刀并没有把右脑变成独立的智能、意识或

cues.en: person, but rather it has always been. In normal people, perhaps right brain grows up as a companion without a choice. Feeling at first somewhat equal partners, but then as speech develops that it can't participate in, that increasingly becomes the central point of life, it resigns to mutely coordinate with left brain. At this moment in your normal head, there are two of you watching this video. One having a mind equals blown moment, and the other mentally rolling its eye at the obviousness of it all.
cues.zh: 人格，而是它本来一直就是。在正常人身上，也许右脑在成长过程中只是个别无选择的伴侣。起初它觉得自己是个平等的伙伴，但随着它无法参与的语言能力不断发展，并逐渐成为生命的核心，它便认命般地默默配合左脑。此时此刻，在你的正常脑袋里，正有两个你在看这个视频。一个正震撼得头脑发懵，另一个则在心里翻白眼，觉得这一切简直显而易见。

cues.en: In split brains, right doesn't freak out because not a whole lot has really changed. You might not agree and may be arguing right now why it can't be possible. Exactly as we would expect talking left brain to do. Speculation aside, split brain patients show at the very least that in the mind there is a separate something that can hear and understand and respond given the right circumstances. Your brain isn't entirely yours.
cues.zh: 在裂脑人中，右脑不会惊慌，因为其实并没有太大变化。你可能不同意，甚至现在就在论证这为什么不可能。这正是我们预期中“会说话的左脑”会做的事。抛开推测不谈，裂脑患者至少表明，心灵中存在某种独立的东西，在合适的情况下能听见、理解并作出回应。你的大脑并不完全属于你。

cues.en: Who is you? You is two. But we can go deeper. You are many. The pile of meat that is your body is made up of trillions of tiny individuals that have a life of their own. So at which point do the many become one? What makes lots of tiny things? You. Click here to go to our channel and watch the next part. Seriously, if you haven't checked out Kurt's Gazette, then you don't know what you're missing. Kurt's Gazette? Kurt's Gazette? I never know.
cues.zh: 你是谁？你是两个。但我们可以再深入。你是许多。你身体这堆肉由数万亿个微小个体组成，它们有自己的生命。那么，从哪一点起，许多变成一个？是什么让许多微小事物成为你？是你。点击这里前往我们的频道，观看下一部分。说真的，如果你还没看过 Kurt's Gazette，那你不知道自己错过了什么。Kurt's Gazette？Kurt's Gazette？我从来搞不清。
